triggers.rationale: Buy level — start the position when the price breaks above $331.00.

60-day business checkpoint: review whether Services growth rate is holding, CEO Ternus has communicated capital-allocation intent, and iPhone 18 cycle is tracking to expectation — confirm thesis is visibly working or articulate what changed.
Q4 FY2026 earnings approaching — re-read thesis against Services growth trajectory, gross margin guidance, and any CEO commentary on capital allocation before the print.
Once up 20%+ from entry, a 15% give-back from the peak is a prompt to name which invalidation condition tripped — do not exit without identifying what broke in the business.
Below the September 9 swing low at $309.90 and under the current pullback structure; a break there would say this base failed, not just wobbled.
Prior analyst bull-case cluster in the $380-$400 range; $385 remains a realistic next upside objective if the 20-day reclaim resolves the base higher.

Gave back 15% from the high. This is a question, not a sale: is the reason we bought still true? If yes, hold and raise the floor under real structure (the 20-day low, the breakout level). If partly, trim. Sell only if you can name what broke in the business.
Gave back 25% from the high — the catastrophe line for a multi-year hold. The review at 15% should have acted long before this; if we are here, protect the capital.
Below the 200-day — the long trend is in question. Review the business, not the chart.
Up 15% from entry — re-underwrite at the new price and raise the floor under real structure (DAV-279 ruling).
Down 15% from entry — decide hold-vs-cut deliberately, before the stop decides (DAV-279 ruling).
Down 7% in a day — evaluate a pullback-add ONLY if the drop is market/sector-wide with the thesis intact. A company-specific drop is thesis damage: do not add — hold, trim, or exit. Approval-gated.
Up 7% in a day — strength on a held name. Evaluate pressing the winner (add + raise target/stop) if the move is thesis-confirming, not an exhaustion spike. Approval-gated.
Look at this every 7 days, counting from the last real review.
Reports within 3 days — decide before the print: hold through it, trim, or wait to add. Size for the gap.
Reported a beat — re-underwrite. A clean beat-and-raise earns a higher target; a beat the stock sold on means the market wanted more.
Reported a miss — is the thesis wrong, or early? Decide deliberately before the stop decides for us.

Filed something material with the SEC — read the filing first; the code says what happened, not whether it's good. A restatement or bankruptcy breaks the numbers; an officer leaving or a deal can change the story.
